result: In a retrospective review of 216 post-COVID rehabilitation outpatients, 15 (6.9%) met Canadian Consensus Criteria for ME/CFS; they were younger, 93% female, had higher baseline FAS (35.8 vs 27.8, p=0.001) that did not improve, and lower baseline 6MWT (479 vs 540 m).
reason: Measures the share of a long COVID cohort meeting ME/CFS criteria, adding a low clinic-based estimate (7%) beside the 4.5% RECOVER and 51% meta-analysis figures; small, retrospective.

result: In 185 long COVID clinic patients, formula-estimated whole blood viscosity was associated with COMPASS-31 score (B=7.0, p=0.01) and with POTS or orthostatic hypotension (23% in the lowest tertile vs 32% in the highest, p=0.04), but not with overall symptom burden (C19-YRSm B=-0.19, p=0.90).
reason: Vascular/autonomic domain: the atlas has no blood viscosity finding. Viscosity was estimated from formulas, not measured, and the study is cross-sectional with no controls.

result: In CSF and serum from neurological long COVID (Yale COVID Mind and EPICC cohorts), brain-tissue immunofluorescence and PhIP-Seq found only sparse, patient-specific reactivities to nuclear and neuronal proteins, with similar overall CSF reactivity frequencies to controls, limited case-control discrimination, and no shared autoantibody signature.
reason: Tests neural autoantibodies directly in long COVID across two cohorts and two compartments and finds no consistent case-control difference; preprint.

result: 49 post-COVID patients with cognitive complaints vs 48 matched healthy controls had broad cognitive deficits, reduced thalamic volumes and reduced bilateral thalamic fractal complexity (with raised occipital and hippocampal fimbria complexity), and lower thalamic complexity correlated with fatigue severity.
reason: Same measure (thalamic MRI structure in long COVID), adds fractal dimensionality and a fatigue correlation; controls were healthy, not specifically recovered.

result: 49 post-COVID patients vs 48 matched healthy controls showed reduced thalamic volume and complexity on MRI, with thalamic complexity tracking fatigue.
reason: This finding concerns structural MRI in ME/CFS; the paper is a long COVID cohort and is already linked correctly to neuro-lc-subcortical-structure.

result: In 150 survivors of severe/critical COVID-19 followed for 3 years (PASC in 26% at 15 months and 3 years), serum complement (C2, C4b, C5), inflammatory (IL-6, sTNFR-1) and endothelial (angiopoietin) biomarkers were not associated with PASC or with PEM, fatigue or brain-fog phenotypes, while frailty and poor physical function were.
reason: Tests complement markers against PASC status longitudinally and finds no association; caveats: post-ARDS population and complement components (C2, C4b, C5) rather than the activation products (TCC, iC3b, Ba, C5a) in the finding.

result: In 150 COVID-19 ARDS survivors, inflammatory, endothelial and complement biomarkers were not associated with PASC over 3 years.
reason: No routine coagulation markers (D-dimer, fibrinogen, PT/APTT) are reported, and the finding is about ME/CFS; the complement result is already linked to vascular-complement-long-covid.

result: A meta-analysis of 11 studies (593 post-COVID patients, 565 healthy controls) found only a non-significant trend toward lower HRV: SDNN SMD 0.26 (95% CI -0.03 to 0.56, p=0.09), rMSSD SMD 0.11 (p=0.41), LF/HF SMD -0.27 (p=0.12), with I2 78-83% and 9 of 11 studies at high risk of bias.
reason: Same measure (resting HRV vs controls) with no significant difference, though in long COVID rather than ME/CFS, so it is a weak null for the long COVID version only.

result: A meta-analysis of 11 studies (593 post-COVID, 565 controls) found non-significant trends toward lower SDNN, rMSSD and LF/HF.
reason: The finding concerns orthostatic testing (initial orthostatic hypotension, POTS) and MSNA, not resting HRV; the paper is already linked to neuro-hrv.

result: In 100 long COVID patients, 82% had abnormal COMPASS-31 and 60% had abnormal HRV, while the NASA lean test found orthostatic hypotension in 12% and POTS in 10%; COMPASS-31 was associated with symptom burden (beta 0.37).
reason: Objective autonomic testing in long COVID finds abnormalities in most patients (HRV 60%), in line with the finding, although orthostatic rates were low on the NASA lean test; no controls, and the cohort probably overlaps with 42007006.
